code:
res = seasonal_decompose(s, model="additive", period=12)

# recovered slope/month:  1.56  (true: 1.5)
# residual std:           2.94  (true noise sd: 4)
# trend has 12 NaNs at the ends (centered moving average)
caption: Built the series ourselves, so we can check decomposition recovers what we put in

code:
additive:       value = trend + seasonal + noise
multiplicative: value = trend * seasonal * noise

# yearly swing, additive:        ~75 in every year
# yearly swing, multiplicative:  ~100 (yr1) -> ~189 (yr5)
caption: If the peaks get taller as the series rises, think multiplicative

code:
from statsmodels.tsa.seasonal import STL
stl = STL(s, period=12).fit()

# stl.trend has NO missing values
# seasonal pattern can change slowly, robust to outliers
caption: Classical decomposition assumes a fixed seasonal shape and leaves gaps -- STL doesn't
